title: Identifiability and Estimation Precision in Quantum Network Tomography with Imperfect Bell-State Measurements
authors: Athira Kalavampara Raghunadhan, Matheus Guedes De Andrade, Don Towsley, Indrakshi Dey, Daniel Kilper, Nicola Marchetti
abstract: We study Quantum Network Tomography (QNT) for end-to-end link-error characterization under imperfect Bell-state measurements (BSMs), where multiplicative coupling between link and measurement parameters makes identifiability non-trivial. For an n-node star network, we design probes that ensure unique identifiability and derive closed-form expressions for the Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) and Maximum Likelihood Estimators (MLEs), and characterize estimation precision through the Cramer-Rao Bound (CRB). The results show that BSM imperfections degrade estimation precision, while the proposed probes maintain nearly stable precision for individual link parameters as the network size increases. Monte Carlo simulations further confirm that the Mean Squared Error (MSE) approaches the CRB with increasing sample size.
summary: This work analyzes Quantum Network Tomography in star networks suffering from imperfect Bell-State Measurements. The authors develop specialized measurement probes to guarantee that all link and noise parameters are uniquely identifiable. They derive theoretical bounds on estimation precision, confirming that the proposed probes maintain stable accuracy even as the network grows.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of characterizing quantum links in Quantum Network Tomography (QNT) when the Bell-State Measurements (BSMs) used are imperfect.
main_result: By designing specific probe sequences, the authors ensure unique parameter identifiability and show that the estimation precision (CRB) remains stable for individual link parameters even as the network size increases.
method: The study uses theoretical analysis involving the Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) and Cramér-Rao Bounds (CRB) to quantify estimation precision, alongside constructing specific probe measurements to ensure parameter identifiability.
model_or_system: The system is an $n$-node star network where links are modeled as depolarizing channels characterized by a quality parameter $w_k$. Imperfections are introduced via a depolarizing channel affecting the BSMs, parameterized by $b$.
key_observables: Link entanglement quality ($w_k$), BSM noise parameter ($b$), Fisher Information Matrix (FIM), and Mean Squared Error (MSE).
important_parameters: Network size ($n$), link parameters ($w_k$), BSM imperfection parameter ($b$), and the number of measurement shots ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is limited to the star network topology, and the initial derivations rely on logarithmic transformations which exclude zero values for $w_k$ and $b$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate probe construction in small networks, show the dependence of CRB on the BSM parameter $b$, and compare empirical MSEs from Monte Carlo simulations against theoretical CRBs as the number of shots increases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the parameter estimation challenges posed by imperfect BSMs, then developing improved probe designs to achieve unique identifiability, and finally deriving the FIM and MLEs to characterize the resulting estimation precision.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous theoretical tools (FIM, CRB) to quantify the limits of measurement in complex quantum systems, which is crucial for designing fault-tolerant quantum communication protocols.
